text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Bank of Lebanon's foreign exchange reserves rose $201.42 million in the second half of November.
-The weekly treasury-bill issue posted a surplus of 374 billion pounds and all yields fell.
-The cabinet will decide on Wednesday whether to call for holding municipal elections or to extend the mandate of the current municipal councils elected more than 30 years ago.
-Israeli war planes fly over eastern city of Baalbek in the Syrian-policed Bekaa Valley.
-The new public school teachers' pay scale costs the treasury about 90 billion pounds per annum, acting Finance Minister Siniora said.
-Economic activity in Lebanon dropped in September and the balance of payments posted a surplus of $36.7 million.
-Foreign currency deposits in commercial banks increased $55.7 million in September.
-Casino de Liban, the biggest gambling and entertainment center in the Middle East before the 1975-90 civil war, will be reopened today by President Hrawi.
-Beirut will ask the countries attending the "Friends of Lebanon" conference in Washington on December 16 to finance 31 infrastructure projects in the country.
-Lebanese troops seized 488 kg (1,074 pounds) of hashish in north Lebanon.
-China's deputy foreign minister meets Lebanese officials.
